Part 3: Automation with the CockroachDB Cloud API

4. Part 3: Automation with the Cloud API

The CockroachDB Cloud API provides programmatic access to cluster management through RESTful HTTP endpoints. It’s ideal for building custom applications, integrating with existing systems, and automating cluster operations that don’t fit the Terraform model.

🧪 Interactive Lab
Follow along with the hands-on lab: CockroachDB Cloud API Lab

4.1. Why Use the Cloud API?

The API enables powerful automation scenarios:

  • Custom Applications: Build your own cluster management tools

  • CI/CD Integration: Deploy clusters as part of deployment pipelines

  • Batch Operations: Create and manage multiple clusters programmatically

  • System Integration: Connect cluster management to existing tools and workflows

  • Reproducibility: Script consistent cluster configurations

While Terraform is recommended for infrastructure-as-code, the API is perfect when you need more flexibility or are integrating with custom systems.

4.2. API Authentication with Service Accounts

The Cloud API uses service accounts for authentication. Service accounts are non-human identities designed for programmatic access.

4.2.1. Creating a Service Account

In the Cloud Console:

  1. Navigate to Organization → Access Management → Service Accounts

  2. Click Create Service Account

  3. Enter name: "training-api"

  4. Enter description: "For API training and automation"

  5. Click Create

4.2.2. Creating an API Key

After creating the service account:

  1. Click Create API Key for your service account

  2. Name it: "training-key"

  3. Click Create

  4. COPY THE SECRET KEY IMMEDIATELY (shown only once!)

  5. Click Done

The API secret format is a long base64-encoded string starting with "CRDB-". Store it securely in a password manager or secrets management system. Never commit it to git!

4.2.3. Assigning Roles

Grant the necessary permissions:

  1. Click Edit Roles on your service account

  2. Enable the Cluster Creator role

  3. Click Update Roles

The Cluster Creator role provides permissions to create, modify, and delete clusters.

4.2.4. Setting Up Environment Variables

Configure your shell environment:

# Set the API secret (replace with your actual secret)
export COCKROACH_API_SECRET="your-api-secret-here"

# Set your initials for unique cluster names
export INITIALS="xyz"

4.2.5. Verifying API Access

Test your authentication with a simple API call:

curl -X GET https://cockroachlabs.cloud/api/v1/clusters \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $COCKROACH_API_SECRET" \
  -H "Cc-Version: 2024-09-16" | jq '.'

If successful, you’ll see a JSON response (empty array [] if you have no clusters). If you get an "unauthorized" error, verify you copied the secret correctly and assigned the Cluster Creator role.

4.3. Creating a Cluster via API

Now let’s create a cluster using the REST API:

curl -X POST https://cockroachlabs.cloud/api/v1/clusters \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $COCKROACH_API_SECRET" \
  -H "Cc-Version: 2024-09-16" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "name": "training-cluster-'$INITIALS'",
    "provider": "GCP",
    "plan": "BASIC",
    "spec": {
      "serverless": {
        "regions": ["us-central1"]
      }
    }
  }' | jq '.' > cluster_info.json

This command:

  • Makes a POST request to the clusters endpoint

  • Authenticates using your API secret

  • Specifies the API version (2024-09-16)

  • Sends JSON cluster configuration

  • Saves the response to cluster_info.json

The JSON configuration defines:

  • name: Unique cluster identifier (with your initials)

  • provider: GCP, AWS, or AZURE

  • plan: BASIC (serverless), STANDARD, or ADVANCED

  • spec.serverless.regions: Array of region codes

4.3.1. Extracting the Cluster ID

The cluster ID is essential for all subsequent operations:

export CLUSTER_ID=$(cat cluster_info.json | jq -r '.id')
echo "Cluster ID: $CLUSTER_ID"

4.3.2. Monitoring Cluster Status

Check the cluster creation progress:

curl -X GET "https://cockroachlabs.cloud/api/v1/clusters/$CLUSTER_ID" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $COCKROACH_API_SECRET" \
  -H "Cc-Version: 2024-09-16" | jq '.state'

The state will progress from CREATING to CREATED (typically 1-2 minutes for Basic clusters).

4.4. Creating a SQL User via API

Create a SQL user to access the database:

curl -X POST "https://cockroachlabs.cloud/api/v1/clusters/$CLUSTER_ID/sql-users" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $COCKROACH_API_SECRET" \
  -H "Cc-Version: 2024-09-16" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "name": "student",
    "password": "cockroachlabs"
  }' | jq '.'

4.5. Getting Connection Information

Retrieve the connection details:

curl -X GET "https://cockroachlabs.cloud/api/v1/clusters/$CLUSTER_ID" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $COCKROACH_API_SECRET" \
  -H "Cc-Version: 2024-09-16" | jq '.regions[0].sql_dns'

This gives you the SQL connection endpoint.

4.6. Connecting to the Cluster

With the connection details, you can connect using the cockroach sql CLI:

# Save the SQL host
export SQL_HOST=$(curl -s -X GET "https://cockroachlabs.cloud/api/v1/clusters/$CLUSTER_ID" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $COCKROACH_API_SECRET" \
  -H "Cc-Version: 2024-09-16" | jq -r '.regions[0].sql_dns')

# Connect
cockroach sql --url "postgresql://student:cockroachlabs@$SQL_HOST:26257/defaultdb?sslmode=require"

4.7. Cleaning Up via API

Delete the cluster when you’re done:

curl -X DELETE "https://cockroachlabs.cloud/api/v1/clusters/$CLUSTER_ID" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $COCKROACH_API_SECRET" \
  -H "Cc-Version: 2024-09-16"

Verify deletion:

curl -X GET https://cockroachlabs.cloud/api/v1/clusters \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $COCKROACH_API_SECRET" \
  -H "Cc-Version: 2024-09-16" | jq '.'

4.8. API Best Practices

When working with the Cloud API:

  • Version Your Requests: Always specify Cc-Version header

  • Secure Your Secrets: Never commit API keys to version control

  • Error Handling: Check HTTP status codes and response messages

  • Rate Limiting: Implement exponential backoff for retries

  • Idempotency: Use cluster names or IDs to avoid duplicates

  • Least Privilege: Create separate service accounts for different purposes

4.9. API Resources Available

The Cloud API supports managing:

  • Clusters (create, read, update, delete)

  • SQL users

  • Databases

  • Private endpoints

  • API keys

  • Service accounts

  • Log export configurations

Explore the full API documentation at: https://www.cockroachlabs.com/docs/api/cloud/v1
